transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

I've been struggling with severe mental distress for about a year now, mostly because of these strange thoughts and delusions where I feel paranoid and watched. I've also been having extreme mood swings where I go from having overflowing energy to feeling deeply depressed, alongside hearing things that aren't there. It has just become too much to handle on my own.
Have you ever experienced the paranoia or heard voices during times when your mood was completely normal, or do they only happen when you are feeling very high or very low?

Yes, actually. There was a period of about two or three weeks where my mood felt completely normal and stable, but I was still hearing those voices and feeling paranoid. It definitely happens even when I'm not feeling super high or really depressed.
During those times when you have overflowing energy, do you also experience things like needing much less sleep, talking very fast, or making impulsive decisions?

Yes, during those high-energy times, I barely need any sleep—often sleeping only a couple of hours or staying up for days while feeling completely refreshed and driven to stay active. I'm not really sure if I talk too fast or make impulsive decisions, but the overflowing energy and lack of sleep are definitely huge for me.
How long do these periods of high energy and decreased sleep typically last when they happen—is it usually just a few days, or does it last for a week or longer?
It lasts much longer than just a few days or a week. This high-energy state with barely any sleep has been going on continuously for about three months now.
You also mentioned going through periods of feeling deeply depressed. When you feel this way, how long do these low periods usually last, and do you lose interest in things you normally enjoy?

Those low, depressed periods typically last for about three months. Instead of just losing interest, I feel completely empty and emotionally numb, while being constantly exhausted both physically and mentally. It leaves me with absolutely no energy to do anything.
Have you recently used any recreational drugs, alcohol, or new medications, or do you have any known medical conditions that could be causing these symptoms?
No, I don't use any recreational drugs, drink alcohol, or take any new medications. I also don't have any known medical conditions that could explain what's been happening.
During those three-month periods of high energy or deep depression, were you also experiencing the paranoid thoughts and hearing voices at the same time?

Yes, absolutely. Even when I was feeling extremely energetic or deeply depressed, the paranoid thoughts and the voices were still there happening at the same time. It felt like there was no break from them, regardless of how my mood shifted.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports a history of both manic (high energy, decreased need for sleep lasting 3 months) and major depressive episodes (lasting 3 months) alongside psychotic symptoms (paranoia and auditory hallucinations). Crucially, the patient experienced a 2-to-3-week period of stable mood during which the psychotic symptoms persisted in the absence of any mood symptoms. This meets the DSM-5 criteria for Schizoaffective Disorder, Bipolar Type, and rules out Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features (where psychosis only occurs during mood episodes) and Schizoaffective Disorder, Depressive Type (due to the presence of manic episodes).
